- IPO proceeds were used to de-lever: the full INR 2,800.00 mn for pre-payment/repayment of the Company's borrowings and the full INR 310.00 mn for repayment of Oswal Solar's borrowings were utilised as on 30.06.2026.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on government policy, subsidy programmes and rural financing schemes — Management states that fluctuations in government policies, subsidy programs and rural financing schemes directly influence demand for pumps, especially in the solar and agricultural segments. Government entities accounted for 76.3% of FY26 revenue and the growth outlook rests on PM-KUSUM, PM-KUSUM 2.0, PM Surya Ghar and state schemes such as Magel Tyala, so any change in scheme design, allocation or timing flows straight through to order inflow.
- Raw material price volatility compressing margins — Rising raw material costs are flagged as an external threat that can impact margins, and the Outlook repeats that the Company is 'mindful of external headwinds, particularly volatility in raw material prices and its potential impact on input costs'. Stainless steel, cast iron and solar cells are the principal inputs.
- Intense competition and price sensitivity in agriculture and rural markets — The Company describes a highly competitive industry where intense competition coupled with price sensitivity in the agriculture and rural markets poses risks to market share.
- Geographic and scheme concentration — Maharashtra contributed 54.9% and Haryana 20.2% of FY26 revenue, so roughly three quarters of revenue rests on two states; management's own FY27 focus is to 'diversify revenue mix away from PM-KUSUM dependence', acknowledging concentration in a single programme and a narrow set of geographies.
- Monsoon and climate dependence creating demand volatility — Dependence on monsoon patterns and climatic conditions is explicitly named as a source of demand volatility for an agriculture-led pump business.
- Technology obsolescence requiring continuous R&D investment — Rapid technological advancements and the growing need for energy-efficient solutions require continuous investment in R&D to stay relevant, per the Opportunities and Threats discussion; smart-monitoring readiness for PM-KUSUM 2.0 is itself a technology qualification requirement.
- Global supply-chain uncertainty and currency fluctuation — Management notes that global uncertainties in supply chains and currency fluctuations may exert additional pressure on operations and profitability.
- Single-segment business concentration — During the year under review the Company's activity fell within one broad segment — various types of Solar, Pumps & Motors — leaving earnings undiversified across business lines while new verticals (industrial pumps, rooftop/utility/C&I solar) are still pre-revenue or nascent.

business.body:
- [Scheme risk] Management flags "the delay in the rollout of PM KUSUM 2.0" as the trigger for diversification, and industry-wide competitive bidding under Magel Tyala as the cause of a 9% fall in realisations.
- [Receivables] The lengthening receivable cycle is attributed to "delays in payments from state nodal agencies"; management expects normalisation over the medium term, leading to lower cash conversion cycle and "in turn, lower interest costs".
- [Accounting change] "Pursuant to amendments in Ind AS 107 and Ind AS 101, suppliers' credit has been reclassified from other current financial liabilities to current borrowings", which affects the total borrowings and net debt series.
- [Market context] The deck cites public sources for India's solar market: FY26 total ~45 GW across all segments, Utility Scale's share ~47%, Rooftop ~20% (PM Surya Ghar driven) and C&I and KUSUM ~17% each, with installed base milestones of "First 50 GW - 11 Years, Next 50 GW - 3 Years, Last 50 GW - 14 Months".

business.body: Oswal Pumps Limited manufactures solar-powered and grid-connected submersible and monoblock pumps, induction and submersible motors, and solar PV modules under the 'Oswal' brand, and delivers complete turnkey solar pumping systems. It serves agricultural, residential, commercial and industrial water-management applications, selling principally to government entities under schemes such as PM-KUSUM and Maharashtra's Magel Tyala, alongside institutional customers, a dealer network and export markets. Operations began in 2003 with low-speed monoblock pumps and have since been extended by continuous backward integration into castings, stampings, plastic mouldings, submersible wires, controllers, motors, mounting structures, BOS and solar modules.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Oswal Pumps runs both manufacturing campuses within a single integrated site at Karnal, Haryana, covering 3,50,000 square metres of land with 2,80,000 square metres of built-up space. The Pumps and Motors Facility (commissioned 2010, campus area 41,076 sq. m.) is described as one of India's largest single-site pump and motor manufacturing complexes, covering investment casting, CNC machining, press operations, stainless steel TIG and spot welding, winding, assembly, painting and packaging. With stainless steel pump utilisation at 95.14% in FY26 against 79.04% in FY25, management states that existing pump manufacturing capacity is at effective maximum output, which is why the pump and motor expansion and automation programme is being executed on an urgent timeline for commissioning during FY27, with the resulting capacity runway intended to underpin FY28 and beyond volume growth. The Solar Module Facility (commissioned 2024, campus area 11,002 sq. m.) currently operates at 570 MW and holds MNRE approval; Phase 1 expansion to 1,570 MW is targeted for Q2 FY27 and funded from IPO proceeds. Beyond module manufacturing, planned backward integrations include aluminium extrusion and EVA encapsulant sheet manufacturing, covering two cost-significant components of solar module production. Backward integration has progressed from cast iron casting and motor winding in 2011, through plastic moulding, submersible wires, aluminium die casting, thrust bearings and packaging by 2022, to solar PV modules by 2024. The capital programme also includes dedicated investment in CNC machining line expansion, automated welding and press operation modernisation to reduce per-unit labour cost and let throughput scale without proportional headcount growth, with full automation commissioning targeted alongside the broader capex completion in FY27. Separately, the Company is diversifying its product portfolio into industrial pumps, helical pumps, boiler feed pumps and chemical pumps, and has begun participating in the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government policy is the primary demand engine: PM-KUSUM's mandate of 14 million pumps, of which roughly 1.17 million had been done till July 2026, leaves substantial runway
- PM-KUSUM 2.0 is expected to be announced and begin scaling in FY27 and management describes it as the next major order inflow inflection for the Company
- PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana has a ₹22,000 crore Union Budget FY2026-27 allocation targeting one crore households, and the Company secured its first order under the scheme in FY26
- Maharashtra's Magel Tyala Saur Krushi Pump Yojana targets 10 lakh solar agricultural pumps by FY2029 with ₹8,096 crore earmarked in the state's FY2025-26 capital expenditure budget
- Structural replacement opportunity: 8 million diesel pumps in Indian farms representing a ₹1,200 billion (US$ 14.5 billion) replacement opportunity, with a combined solar-pump market potential of approximately ₹3,600 billion
- Indian solar pump market grew from INR 1.7B in FY19 to INR 164.5B in FY25 and is expected to reach INR 271.1B by FY30 at an 11.0% CAGR, expected to account for around 57% of the total pumps market by FY30
- Indian industrial pump market growing at 11.8% CAGR toward FY30, offering a less-seasonal, higher-margin segment for entry
- Backward integration into modules, structures, BOS, aluminium extrusion and EVA encapsulant is the stated cost and quality lever, with automation reducing per-unit labour cost and allowing throughput to scale without proportional headcount growth
- Aftermarket and service network is described as a pillar of recurring revenue and durable customer relationships
- Headwinds management flags: volatility in raw material prices and its potential impact on input costs, intense competition and price sensitivity in agriculture and rural markets, dependence on government policy and subsidy programmes, monsoon dependence, and global supply-chain and currency uncertainty
- Order book of 22,025 solar pumping systems as at July 31, 2026, with an additional near-term pipeline of over 12,500 pumps, described as providing strong revenue visibility for FY27
- Order book composition as on July 31, 2026 spans Government of Maharashtra (Magel Tyala), Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Ladakh and Madhya Pradesh, other indirect orders, and export orders
- Rooftop Solar, Utility and C&I Solar EPC order book of approximately 72 MW as on August 07, 2026, against a wider pipeline of 359 MW and 1,474 MW of open tenders
- Exports: 3,000 pump units in the current order book (also cited as 3,400 pump units in the Chairman's market-opportunity commentary)
- First order secured under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana in FY26; a 63 MW Bihar rooftop project and a Rajasthan HAM SPV are cited in the projects and institutional channel

deepdive.thesis: Oswal Pumps delivered record FY26 profitability (PAT +34% YoY) driven by PM-KUSUM execution, but guides for a back-ended FY27 (20-25% growth) due to timing gaps before PM-KUSUM 2.0 rollout. Strategic diversification into rooftop/C&I solar and deep backward integration (modules, upcoming inverters) aims to de-risk single-scheme dependency, though near-term margins face pressure from geopolitical input costs and competitive tendering.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Oswal Pumps Limited manufactures solar-powered and grid-connected submersible and monoblock pumps, induction and submersible motors, and solar PV modules under the 'Oswal' brand, and delivers complete turnkey solar pumping systems. It serves agricultural, residential, commercial and industrial water-management applications, selling principally to government entities under schemes such as PM-KUSUM and Maharashtra's Magel Tyala, alongside institutional customers, a dealer network and export markets. Operations began in 2003 with low-speed monoblock pumps and have since been extended by continuous backward integration into castings, stampings, plastic mouldings, submersible wires, controllers, motors, mounting structures, BOS and solar modules.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government policy is the primary demand engine: PM-KUSUM's mandate of 14 million pumps, of which roughly 1.17 million had been done till July 2026, leaves substantial runway
- PM-KUSUM 2.0 is expected to be announced and begin scaling in FY27 and management describes it as the next major order inflow inflection for the Company

- Maharashtra's Magel Tyala Saur Krushi Pump Yojana targets 10 lakh solar agricultural pumps by FY2029 with ₹8,096 crore earmarked in the state's FY2025-26 capital expenditure budget
- Structural replacement opportunity: 8 million diesel pumps in Indian farms representing a ₹1,200 billion (US$ 14.5 billion) replacement opportunity, with a combined solar-pump market potential of approximately ₹3,600 billion
- Indian solar pump market grew from INR 1.7B in FY19 to INR 164.5B in FY25 and is expected to reach INR 271.1B by FY30 at an 11.0% CAGR, expected to account for around 57% of the total pumps market by FY30
- Indian industrial pump market growing at 11.8% CAGR toward FY30, offering a less-seasonal, higher-margin segment for entry
- Backward integration into modules, structures, BOS, aluminium extrusion and EVA encapsulant is the stated cost and quality lever, with automation reducing per-unit labour cost and allowing throughput to scale without proportional headcount growth
- Aftermarket and service network is described as a pillar of recurring revenue and durable customer relationships
- Headwinds management flags: volatility in raw material prices and its potential impact on input costs, intense competition and price sensitivity in agriculture and rural markets, dependence on government policy and subsidy programmes, monsoon dependence, and global supply-chain and currency uncertainty
- Order book of 22,025 solar pumping systems as at July 31, 2026, with an additional near-term pipeline of over 12,500 pumps, described as providing strong revenue visibility for FY27
- Order book composition as on July 31, 2026 spans Government of Maharashtra (Magel Tyala), Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Ladakh and Madhya Pradesh, other indirect orders, and export orders
- Rooftop Solar, Utility and C&I Solar EPC order book of approximately 72 MW as on August 07, 2026, against a wider pipeline of 359 MW and 1,474 MW of open tenders

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Oswal Pumps runs both manufacturing campuses within a single integrated site at Karnal, Haryana, covering 3,50,000 square metres of land with 2,80,000 square metres of built-up space. The Pumps and Motors Facility (commissioned 2010, campus area 41,076 sq. m.) is described as one of India's largest single-site pump and motor manufacturing complexes, covering investment casting, CNC machining, press operations, stainless steel TIG and spot welding, winding, assembly, painting and packaging. With stainless steel pump utilisation at 95.14% in FY26 against 79.04% in FY25, management states that existing pump manufacturing capacity is at effective maximum output, which is why the pump and motor expansion and automation programme is being executed on an urgent timeline for commissioning during FY27, with the resulting capacity runway intended to underpin FY28 and beyond volume growth. The Solar Module Facility (commissioned 2024, campus area 11,002 sq. m.) currently operates at 570 MW and holds MNRE approval; Phase 1 expansion to 1,570 MW is targeted for Q2 FY27 and funded from IPO proceeds. Beyond module manufacturing, planned backward integrations include aluminium extrusion and EVA encapsulant sheet manufacturing, covering two cost-significant components of solar module production. Backward integration has progressed from cast iron casting and motor winding in 2011, through plastic moulding, submersible wires, aluminium die casting, thrust bearings and packaging by 2022, to solar PV modules by 2024. The capital programme also includes dedicated investment in CNC machining line expansion, automated welding and press operation modernisation to reduce per-unit labour cost and let throughput scale without proportional headcount growth, with full automation commissioning targeted alongside the broader capex completion in FY27. Separately, the Company is diversifying its product portfolio into industrial pumps, helical pumps, boiler feed pumps and chemical pumps, and has begun participating in the Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana.

ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
